gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has big, round, glassy openings. Nippo goes the other way, its thin wire-cut strokes all one width and its small letters nearly as tall as capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Nippo draws its curves in wire-like strokes that never thin at the shoulders, with small letters standing almost as tall as capitals. Noto Sans Grantha is the plain sans below, tall and open, and if you shrink the heading it loses its edge while this body would feel oversized.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Spaghetti-thin strokes of one uniform thickness give Nippo a technical, wire-cut look, with small letters standing almost as tall as capitals. Noto Sans Gujarati is the sans-serif that follows, its curves stopping short and its counters wide.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-gondi: Wire-bent and technical. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi brings chunky, crayon-tall lowercase with generous gaps at the stroke ends, while Nippo's thin round letters hover above it like a bent filament over a sturdy base.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Nippo's rounds and stems share one gauge, like cut wire. Noto Sans Gurmukhi sits beneath it as a sans with outward-pointing terminals and short ascenders, so the thin technical heading and the sturdier text feel like two different machines.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Nippo looks like tubing cut to length, with small letters standing almost capital-high. Its job is large and brief, where its stems and curves of one gauge can be admired, while Noto Sans Hanunoo is the sans with open terminals underneath.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew fills most of each line with its tall midsection and leaves wide gaps where curves meet stems. Nippo sits against it like a ruler-straight wire next to a softer, fuller line.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-hk: Technical, a bit like bent wire, is how Nippo comes across, with curves and straights all one width. Noto Sans HK is the plain sans that follows, its large lowercase and lifted brush ends making a long paragraph feel open and unhurried.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-imperial-arama: Fat crossbars, wire-cut strokes, almost-capital lowercase. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic takes over as a sans with its c ends flung apart like pincers, so Nippo's chunky joins and the body's open shapes sit together comfortably.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-inscriptional-: Nippo draws its stems and crossbars at a single thickness, like cut wire, with small letters standing almost as tall as capitals. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is a sans with big open eyes and a deep middle band, which keeps long text easy going.
